name: Dipesh Kumar
punch: Building resilient UI frameworks and thoughtful software systems.
intro: I build core desktop UI frameworks at Microsoft — [WPF](https://github.com/dotnet/wpf) and [WinUI 3](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/winui/), used by 700K+ developers behind apps like Visual Studio, AutoCAD, and Microsoft Store — while exploring developer tooling, language models, and visual design.
about: I'm Dipesh Kumar, a Software Engineer II at Microsoft in Hyderabad with 5+ years on the core team of [Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF)](https://github.com/dotnet/wpf) and [WinUI 3](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/winui/). Maintaining foundational .NET and Windows UI frameworks in the open ([@dipeshmsft](https://github.com/dipeshmsft)) means balancing decades-long compatibility with modern API design, community PR reviews, and open-source leadership.

Across my work at Microsoft and research at IIT (BHU) Varanasi, I enjoy moving across layers — from reactive UI controls, ETL/Kusto performance pipelines, and AI-assisted servicing agents to VS Code developer extensions, C++ OpenGL rendering, and published NLP research on subword tokenization.

Outside of engineering, you'll usually find me reading fiction or essays over a cup of chai, experimenting with typography and visual design, or out on road trips and mountain trails with a camera — moments I collect in the [Gallery](/gallery/).

details: Spearheaded the Windows 11 native Fluent theme and runtime theme-switching infrastructure for [WPF](https://github.com/dotnet/wpf) — introducing [Fluent ThemeMode](https://github.com/dotnet/wpf/issues/8932) and [AccentColor](https://github.com/dotnet/wpf/issues/9295) APIs, and shipping [WPF Gallery on Microsoft Store](https://www.microsoft.com/store/productId/9NDLX60WX4KQ?ocid=pdpshare) (>20K downloads) to showcase the new controls and themes.

Engineered a performant reactive data pipeline for the [WinUI 3](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/winui/) TableView control (filtering, grouping, sorting, and live change tracking across flat and hierarchical data) and owned end-to-end delivery of SplitMenuFlyoutItem.

Authored a WinUI performance measurement dashboard (latency, memory, and scroll metrics extracted from ETL traces into Azure Data Explorer / Kusto) and rejuvenated WinUI Snoop for real-time visual-tree and property inspection without debugger setup.

Built an internal AI agent for the WPF servicing workflow to adapt fixes across framework versions, build constraints, and version-control systems (TFVC, Source Depot) — reducing manual effort by 75%.

Designed the [OpenFolderDialog API](https://github.com/dotnet/wpf/issues/7689) in WPF (.NET 8) — a top-voted community request (>170 upvotes) — delivering integration tests, developer documentation, and an official [.NET Blog article](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/wpf-file-dialog-improvements-in-dotnet-8/).

Investigated and resolved critical production issues for enterprise clients (Visual Studio, Affinity, Siemens Healthcare, Schneider Electric), improving reliability for 1M+ professionals across healthcare and design.

Led open-sourcing of the [dotnet/wpf](https://github.com/dotnet/wpf) test suite and infrastructure, building automated sanitization workflows and enabling CI-based unit testing for faster PR ingestion.
Extended an internal hardware debug tool aggregating on-board power and thermal data with command polling, telemetry parsers, and a live visualization dashboard.
Built REST API endpoints for Android clients and redesigned PostgreSQL review schemas using Django REST Framework.
